edges.description: The recurrent BANF1 p.Ala12Thr substitution directly disrupts the DNA-binding surface of BAF.
Depletion and defective DNA binding of BAF perturb nuclear lamina organization and emerin localization.
Impaired DNA binding perturbs normal BAF-mediated nuclear envelope-chromatin tethering.
Chronic nuclear lamina and chromatin dysfunction drives severe progressive osteolysis and generalized osteoporosis.
Combined lipoatrophy, craniofacial bone resorption, and skin atrophy produce a pseudosenile progeroid appearance.
Nuclear and chromatin dysregulation contributes to postnatal somatic growth retardation.
Chronic connective-tissue and periarticular dysfunction produces progressive joint stiffness.
BANF1-related nuclear and chromatin dysregulation contributes to the progeroid habitus, including reduced subcutaneous adipose tissue.
Generalized resorptive bone loss and dysplastic remodeling manifest clinically as profound skeletal abnormalities.
Focal and regional bone resorption causes marked osteolysis of the mandible, maxilla, clavicles, ribs, and distal phalanges.
Generalized bone loss produces severe early-onset osteoporosis.
Severe mandibular osteolysis causes progressive mandibular regression and micrognathia.
Maxillary/orbital bone resorption and loss of periorbital fat produce prominent eyes (proptosis).
Axial skeletal osteopenia and structural bone remodeling lead to severe scoliosis.
